How to assess: Use an entirely fictional equipment installation task to check whether you can document leveling and alignment points, assembly sequence, energy isolation steps, trial-run checks, and recording requirements, retaining reviewable records.
Suitable conditions: Willingness to follow procedures on-site and around equipment, complete leveling, alignment, and assembly, troubleshoot systematically, and maintain energy isolation.

entries: Installation and alignment: Read drawings and measure, using instruments to level, establish centerlines, and assemble components.
Repair and troubleshooting: Dismantle and service equipment, perform weld repairs, and diagnose mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical faults.

paragraphs: Millwrights corresponds to O*NET 49-9044.00. Duties involve installing, dismantling, repairing, and calibrating industrial machinery and equipment, including leveling and alignment, component assembly, weld repairs, and troubleshooting.
Work context (O*NET work context survey): 55% work in cramped or awkward spaces at least weekly, 41% bend or twist continually, and 36% work at height at least monthly.

Pace and responsibility: 36% rate repeating the same tasks as very important, and 45% bear high responsibility for others' work results. Work often requires coordination with production, construction, and other trades.
Abilities and work practices: Machinery and equipment knowledge, drawing interpretation and measurement skills, procedural safety practices, and honest recording.
Main outputs: Equipment condition after installation or repair, alignment and trial-run records, and repair and isolation records.

Key judgments concern whether equipment meets alignment and operating requirements, whether faults are clearly diagnosed, and whether work occurs only after energy isolation and protection are in place.
Verify Chinese job titles and authority by industry, task, and location.

Adjacent relationships are for comparing directions only. This occupation centers on installation, alignment, and whole-machine repair. Industrial machinery mechanics focus on routine maintenance, general repair workers cover more broadly but less deeply, machinists make parts, and electricians focus on electrical systems. Qualifications and safety requirements are not interchangeable.
Compare each point: Who handles installation and alignment, who handles routine maintenance, who holds special-operation qualifications, and who bears acceptance responsibility?
Difference from industrial machinery mechanics: They focus on routine maintenance and repairs; this occupation focuses on installation, alignment, and calibration.
Difference from machinists: They mainly machine parts; this occupation focuses on equipment installation and whole-machine repair.
Difference from electricians: They focus on electrical systems; this occupation focuses on mechanical installation and alignment.

risks.consequence: Affects traceability and later repair judgments.

risks.affected_roles: Workers, team leaders, and safety leads.
risks.consequence: Can prevent continued work before risks are removed.
risks.mitigation: Retain records and escalate through the process.
risks.scenario: Shared escalation rule: For energy isolation, lifting, alignment, or equipment abnormalities, first stop work and isolate risks. Refer facts and unresolved questions to authorized people before continuing.
risks.title: Abnormality work stoppage and handover
